deep.reconstruction:
The page holds three unrelated memoranda, and only the last involves any computation.

(1) 'Steffens Vorlesungen in Berlin im Hause des Generals von Gneisenau' records a book or lecture series: Henrik Steffens' lectures given in Berlin in the house of General Gneisenau. It is followed by a pointing-hand sign that refers to the entries below or on the facing page.

(2) Bibliographic notes.
(a) 'Journal de l'école normale. Fourier's Definition der Ebne. Lacroix I. p. 503.' This points to Fourier's proposed definition of the plane in the discussions of the École normale of 1795 (Séances des écoles normales, debates with Monge). Fourier defined the plane as the locus of points equidistant from two given points. Lacroix reports this in vol. I, p. 503 of one of his works.
(b) 'Memorie della reale accademia delle scienze di Torino, T. XXIV, Damoiseau sur la comète de 1769 [prob. 1759], G. G. A. 1821 p. 1685.' This cites Damoiseau's memoir in the Turin Memoirs, vol. 24, together with the review of it in the Göttingische gelehrte Anzeigen, 1821, p. 1685. If the comet is that of 1759, the memoir is Damoiseau's prize computation of the 1835 return of Halley's comet.
These reflect Gauss's known interests in the foundations of geometry (the definition of the plane) and in cometary perturbation theory.

(3) Instrument note: 'An Ertelschen 8 z[ölligen] Theodolithen hatten die Gewinde der ursprünglichen Stellschrauben eine Weite von 0.3125 mm = 5/16 Millim. Einer Umdrehung entspricht daher eine Bewegung von ca 10 Minuten.' In words: on Ertel's 8-inch theodolites the original levelling (foot) screws had a thread pitch of p = 0.3125 mm = 5/16 mm, so one turn tilts the instrument by about 10 arcminutes.
- The implicit step (my reconstruction): one full turn raises the screw tip by p. Over a lever arm L (distance from the screw to the opposite support or pivot) this gives a tilt θ = arctan(p/L) ≈ p/L in radians.
- For θ = 10' = 0.0029089 rad we need L = p/θ ≈ 107.4 mm.
- That is almost exactly 4 Paris inches (108.27 mm), the half-diameter of an 8-inch circle. With L = 108.27 mm one gets θ ≈ 9.92', i.e. 'ca 10 Minuten'.
- So the note implicitly takes the lever arm to be about 4 Paris inches.
errors: No errors in the arithmetic: 5/16 = 0.3125 exactly.
The 10' claim is only approximate and depends on an unstated lever arm of about 107-108 mm (≈4 Paris inches). This is consistent with an 8-inch instrument.
Possible slip: the comet date may be 1759 (Halley's comet, which was Damoiseau's Turin prize subject) rather than 1769. The digit is ambiguous in the image.
